# Story 12 — Live chat

## Prerequisites

- Story 04 completed (`crm-mvp`, merged to `main`): `apps/tickets/{models,views,serializers}.py`,
  `TicketMessage`, the agent `messages` action.
- Story 05 completed (`crm-mvp`): `apps/portal/{models,views,serializers}.py`, the portal
  `messages` action, `PortalTicketCreateSerializer`.
- Story 08/09 completed (`crm-mvp`): `frontend/src/routes/PortalHome.tsx`,
  `frontend/src/features/portal/{SubmitTicket,PortalTicketDetail}.tsx`.
- Story 07 completed (`crm-mvp`): `frontend/src/features/tickets/TicketDetail.tsx`.
- **No new dependencies.** No Django Channels, no Redis, no WebSocket library. Confirmed against
  the intake: this story's only genuinely new mechanism is a `refetchInterval` on two existing
  TanStack Query hooks, scoped to `channel === "chat"` tickets only.

---

## Story Goal

Close the last unimplemented item in the requirements PDF's "Communication Channels" area: **Live
chat**. Give the portal a "Start a live chat" entry point that creates (or reuses) a
`channel: "chat"` ticket and drops the customer straight into its conversation view; make that
same conversation view — on both the portal side and the agent side — poll for new messages every
few seconds while a chat-channel ticket is open, so a back-and-forth conversation feels live
without a manual reload. Every other channel (email, whatsapp, sms, web) is untouched and keeps
today's fetch-once behavior.

No new message model, no new message-sending endpoint — `TicketMessage` and its two existing
`messages` actions (agent and portal) already accept and store `channel: "chat"` messages
correctly today; confirmed in Context below.

**File: `backend/apps/portal/tests/`** — add to the file already covering

```python
@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_a_portal_ticket_can_be_created_as_a_chat_channel_ticket(portal_client, ...):
    response = portal_client.post(
        "/api/v1/portal/tickets/",
        {"subject": "Live chat started", "description": "Live chat started", "channel": "chat"},
    )
    assert response.status_code == 201
    ticket = Ticket.objects.get(pk=response.data["id"])
    assert ticket.channel == "chat"
```

No backend code changes are expected to make this pass — `PortalTicketCreateSerializer` already
accepts `channel` (Context item 5). If this test fails, that is the one real backend bug this
story would need to fix; do not add a bypass or a second field to work around it without first
confirming why the existing field isn't behaving as documented.

### 2 — Wire `channel` through `useSubmitPortalTicket`

**File: `frontend/src/api/portal.ts`** lines 84–100 — widen the mutation's args type and
`toFormData` call:

```typescript
mutationFn: (args: {
  subject: string;

    .post<{ id: number; number: string }>(
      "/portal/tickets/",
      toFormData(

          subject: args.subject,
          description: args.description,
          category: args.category,

      { headers: { "Content-Type": "multipart/form-data" } },

    .then((r) => r.data),
```

`channel` is **optional** on the args type and only added to the form body when present —
`SubmitTicket.tsx`'s existing call (Context item 10, line 86) does not pass it and must keep
creating `web`-channel tickets exactly as it does today (the model's own `default=Channel.WEB`

### 3 — Scoped polling on the two message hooks

**File: `frontend/src/api/tickets.ts`** lines 74–80:

```typescript
export const useTicketMessages = (id: number | null, live: boolean = false) =>
  useQuery({
    queryKey: qk.tickets.messages(id ?? 0),
    queryFn: () =>
      api.get<TicketMessage[]>(`/tickets/${id}/messages/`).then((r) => r.data),
    enabled: id !== null,
    // The codebase's first polling query — deliberately scoped to `live`
    // (the caller passes `ticket.channel === "chat"`), not a global default.
    // Every other channel's conversation tab keeps the old fetch-once
    // behavior. `refetchIntervalInBackground` stays at its default `false`,
    // so this also stops the moment the tab is backgrounded — no extra code.
    refetchInterval: live ? 4000 : false,
  });
```

**File: `frontend/src/features/tickets/TicketDetail.tsx`** line 69:

```typescript
const { data: messages, isPending: messagesPending } = useTicketMessages(
  ticket.id,
  ticket.channel === "chat",
);
```

**File: `frontend/src/api/portal.ts`** lines 107–112, same shape:

```typescript
export const usePortalMessages = (id: number | null, live: boolean = false) =>
  useQuery({
    queryKey: qk.portal.tickets.messages(id ?? 0),
    queryFn: () => api.get<PortalMessage[]>(`/portal/tickets/${id}/messages/`).then((r) => r.data),
    enabled: id !== null,
    refetchInterval: live ? 4000 : false,
  });
```

**File: `frontend/src/features/portal/PortalTicketDetail.tsx`** line 101:

### 4 — "Start a live chat" entry point

**File: `frontend/src/routes/PortalHome.tsx`**

Add a handler and a second button next to the existing "Submit a request" one (line 63–71 block):

```tsx
const submitChat = useSubmitPortalTicket();

const onStartLiveChat = () => {
  const existing = open.find((ticket) => ticket.channel === "chat");
  if (existing) {
    navigate(`/portal/tickets/${existing.id}`);
    return;
  }
  submitChat.mutate(
    {
      subject: t("portal.liveChatSubject"),
      description: t("portal.liveChatSubject"),
      category: null,
      channel: "chat",
      attachments: [],
    },
    {
      onSuccess: (created) => navigate(`/portal/tickets/${created.id}`),
      onError: () => toast.error(t("portal.submitFailed")),
    },
  );
};
```

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-3">
  <h1 className="text-[22px] font-bold tracking-[-0.01em]">{t("portal.home")}</h1>
  <div className="flex gap-2">
    <Button variant="outline" data-testid="start-live-chat" onClick={onStartLiveChat} disabled={submitChat.isPending}>
      <MessageSquare aria-hidden className="h-4 w-4" />
      {t("portal.startLiveChat")}
    </Button>
    <Button asChild data-testid="submit-request">
      <Link to="/portal/new">
        <Plus aria-hidden className="h-4 w-4" />
        {t("portal.submitRequest")}
      </Link>
    </Button>
  </div>
</div>
```

Import `MessageSquare` from `lucide-react` (matching `ChannelBadge.tsx`'s own chat icon, Context
item 13) and `useSubmitPortalTicket` from `@/api/portal`; reuse whatever toast helper
`SubmitTicket.tsx` line 89 already imports (`toast.error`) — do not add a second toast mechanism.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend tests:** `docker compose exec api pytest -q` — all green, including the new
   channel-on-create test.
2. **Frontend tests:** `cd frontend && npm run test -- --run` — all green, including the two new
   polling-scope tests and the two new "Start a live chat" tests.
3. **Guards:** `npm run check:rtl`, `npm run check:i18n`, `npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit`,
   `npm run build` — all clean.
4. **Live, in the browser — the actual back-and-forth:**
   - Log in to the portal as `customer@demo`, click "Start a live chat", confirm it lands on a new
     ticket's conversation view with no subject/description form ever shown.
   - Click it a second time (new tab or after navigating away) — confirm it reuses the same ticket
     rather than creating a second one.
   - In a separate session, log in as an agent, open that same ticket (findable via its `Live chat`
     `ChannelBadge` in the queue), send a reply. Confirm the customer's portal tab shows the new
     message within ~4 seconds **without reloading the page**.
   - Send a message from the portal side; confirm the agent's Conversation tab shows it within
     ~4 seconds, same way.
5. **Regression — other channels stay untouched:** open a `channel: "email"` (or any non-chat)
   ticket's Conversation tab, confirm no `GET /tickets/{id}/messages/` request fires again on its
   own after the initial load (watch the network tab for ~15 seconds) — the polling must not have
   leaked to other channels.
6. **`docker compose exec api pytest -q` and the frontend suite together** one final time after all
   changes, to catch any interaction between Backend Task 1 and the frontend changes.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] A portal ticket can be created with `channel: "chat"` through the existing
      `PortalTicketCreateSerializer` — proven by a new backend test, not just asserted from reading
      the serializer.
- [ ] `useSubmitPortalTicket` accepts an optional `channel`, defaulting to omitted (still `web` by
      the model's own default) — `SubmitTicket.tsx`'s existing call is unmodified and still creates
      `web`-channel tickets.
- [ ] `useTicketMessages` and `usePortalMessages` each gain an optional `live` parameter
      (default `false`) that sets `refetchInterval: 4000` only when `true`; the one existing call
      site of each passes `ticket.channel === "chat"` (or `ticket?.channel === "chat"` on the
      portal side).
- [ ] A non-chat ticket's conversation view polls exactly as it does today (no new requests without
      a user action) — proven by a frontend test with fake timers, not just by inspection.
- [ ] Portal home has a "Start a live chat" button, distinct from "Submit a request", that reuses an
      existing open chat ticket if one exists and otherwise creates one and navigates straight into
      its conversation view with no ticket-creation form ever shown to the customer.
- [ ] `en.json`/`ar.json` key parity holds (`npm run check:i18n` passes) for the two new keys.
- [ ] No Django Channels, WebSockets, Redis, or any new runtime dependency was added.
- [ ] `docs/00-project-brief.md` / `docs/SUMMARY.md`'s Communication Channels coverage note is
      updated once this ships — Live chat moves from "label only" to "real"; Email/WhatsApp/SMS
